# Global Academic Presence & Rankings
RMIT University, with campuses in **Melbourne (four locations)** and global hubs in **Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, and Malaysia** , ranks **#199–300 globally (QS 2024–2026)** and **14th nationally** , excelling in **applied research in design, technology, and sustainability** . Harvard University, founded in **1636** , dominates globally with **#1 (Academic Ranking, THE-QS since 2003)** , **#3 (QS 2025)** , and **#5 (THE 2025)** , boasting a **$50.7B endowment** and a legacy of **100+ Nobel laureates** and **14 U.S. Presidents** . Peking University ranks **#14 (QS 2025) and #13 (THE 2025)** , leading in **STEM, humanities, and social sciences** , while Harvard’s **Harvard Business School** and Peking’s **Mathematics/Physics programs** are globally preeminent.

# Campus & Structural Evolution
**RMIT** operates across **Melbourne (City, Bundoora, Brunswick, Williams)** and global locations like **Barcelona** , governed by the **RMIT Council** and spanning **four Colleges** . **Boston College** features a **175-acre Gothic-style Chestnut Hill campus** with expansions to **Newton (Law), Brighton (Theology), and Brookline (Messina College, 2024)** , funded by a **$1B budget** and aiming for a **$3B fundraising goal** . **Peking University** combines historic imperial gardens (e.g., **Weiming Lake** ) with modern facilities, including branches in **Beijing, Hanzhong, Shenzhen** , and the **Shenzhen Graduate School (founded 2001)** . **Harvard’s** sprawling **18,000-acre Harvard Yard** and **150+ buildings** —including **Harvard Library (20.4M+ volumes)** —contrast with its **Gothic Revival architecture** , with modern expansions in **Allston (HBS), Longwood (medical schools), and global hubs (D.C., Italy, China)** .

# Academic Reputation & Student Outcomes
**RMIT** achieves **71.8% undergrad employment** within six months, with alumni like **Lydia Lassila (Olympic skier)** and **Mai Phương Thúy (Miss Vietnam)** . **Boston College** admits **15.9%** of applicants (Class of 2028) with a **diverse student body (50 states + 75 countries)** , producing **3 Rhodes and 22 Truman scholars** . **Peking University** ranks **#1 in Asia** , **top 15 globally** , and hosts **~7,000 international students** with dual-degree programs (e.g., **Waseda, Cornell, Yale, Stanford** ). **Harvard** maintains a **6% admit rate** , **40% international students** , and **100+ Nobel laureates** , including **14 U.S. Presidents** and **199 Nobel Prize winners** (most of any institution).

# Research, Collections & Cultural Engagement
**RMIT** focuses on **industry-aligned research** in design, health, and sustainability, with libraries like **Swanston Library** . **Boston College** emphasizes **Jesuit scholarship** , housing **12M+ items** in its **8 research libraries** , including rare manuscripts (Galileo, Ignatius of Loyola). **Peking University** leads in **7 State Key Laboratories** and **Nobel-winning research** (e.g., **Tu Youyou’s artemisinin discovery** ), with collections like the **Sackler Museum** . **Harvard’s** **20.4M-volume library** and **Harvard Art Museums** (150,000+ works) drive interdisciplinary research, from the **Human Genome Project** to **divestment campaigns** .

# Student Life & Demographics
**RMIT** historically prioritizes **STEM majors** with a **global vocational focus** , while **Boston College** boasts a **diverse student body (50% White, 11% Hispanic, 10% Asian)** and **Messina College (2024)** targets first-gen students. **Peking University** attracts a **diverse global cohort** , with **137 undergraduate majors** and **dual-degree programs** . **Harvard’s** **~7,000 undergrads (50% women)** and **15,000+ graduate students** reflect **top-tier diversity** , including **33% White, 22% Asian, and 17% low-income students** .

# Athletics, Traditions & Controversies
**Boston College** competes in **NCAA Division I (ACC)** , with traditions like the **"Golden Eagles"** and **"For Boston"** fight song. **Harvard’s** **NCAA Division I (Big House) and Division III (Harvard Crimson)** teams include **Fenway Park (1912)** and **Harvard Stadium (1914)** , with rivalries like **Harvard-Cornell ice hockey** and **Harvard-McGill rugby** . **Controversies** include **Harvard’s 1923 "Jewish quotas"** , **2016 slavery exhibits** , and **2025 funding cuts** , while **Boston College** faced **racism incidents (2017–2018)** .

# Cultural & Intellectual Influence
Harvard’s **elite tradition** permeates **literature (e.g.,** ***The Sound and the Fury*** **)** , **film (e.g.,** ***The Social Network*** **)** , and **global influence** , with alumni shaping **politics, business, and science** . Its **Nobel laureates, presidents, and billionaires** underscore its unparalleled prestige, while **Peking University’s** **Nobel-winning research** and **imperial legacy** define its academic rigor. **Boston College’s** **Jesuit values** and **Boston College Law Review** highlight its scholarly depth, whereas **RMIT’s** **industry-aligned research** bridges academia and innovation.
